title: Three Times Over the Basket

arc.title: The Cold Stone
arc.subtitle: a warm stone, already going cold

epigraph.text: A figure read thrice is three figures and no account; the silt comes when it comes and asks no leave of the slate.
epigraph.attribution: A saying of the Low Kiln basket-women at the Cross

pov: Daniel Marchetti (Corin), close third-person past tense inside a body of four hundred and twenty-three to four hundred and twenty-five days, six months and two hundred and forty-three to two hundred and forty-five days, carried everywhere in a basket and told by nobody; count 422 exact at the opening on answer 420, closing at 425 exact on answer 426. The old life rides the surgeon's register alone: no present-tense break is spent in this chapter and no \memory{} tag is used, the white room, the page over the speakers and the hands that stayed in the field going on gathering interest from Chapter 113. No departure from the boy's eyes: the Debt Loft is a sound from above and behind, the back room a shape and a dust, the Drawing a room seen and not entered, the out-of-line landing a report brought up the yard and never a sighting, the Cross a square entered only at the third reading with the basket set in the moot-post's finger's width of shade. Ilmen 29 is an ordinary tending day, Ilmen 30 the month's third and last Account-day and market, and Silt 1 the first day of a month come on without a boundary drawn and with neither of the district's two habits of naming its months set right or left; each day has its own dated \daymark and two full scenes of at least eight hundred words. There is no market, no Cross, no bell, no Account-day, no called collector and no runner on Ilmen 29; Ilmen 30's third reading comes by its own morning and three readings of the year stand behind one unsigned figure, three being three and not one account, the figure read still not the figure paid; nothing from that reading crosses into Silt 1 as sign, lesson, mending, cause, payment or payer. The two sightings at the Ilmen 30 market — a woman with clay under her nails and a pale cord-mark on the back of one hand who turns a cup a quarter and sets it back where it stood, and a foundling at the edge who turns his head a half-beat after a note — are two sightings on separate trays, never Fenna or Ulda in the narration, with no loaf, slate, sale, word or name passing between them and no eighth of either, planted years ahead and unspent.
places: the flat stone by the well
the reading block under the moot-post
the moot-post's finger's width of shade

scenes.title: The Twenty-ninth Morning
scenes.synopsis: First entry, the chapter's only \dropcap and its first dated \daymark{423}{Ilmen 29, Y.H. 814, Ninthday}: small hours opening on the hand laid flat on the fold on answer 420 and the count exact at 422, six months and two hundred and forty-two days told by nobody, then first light, the carrying-down and the morning work of an ordinary Ninthday with no market, Cross, bell or reading. Present: Corin/Dan, Sella Vail at the hearth before the basket, Tarn at the kindling and flagstones, Jorra Vail at the wheel-shed edge; Garl Vail in objects only. Ilva offstage with her count still in wood, Hessa's slate unread up the road and Berr up the clay road with the box locked; no offered figure repeated, no well-telling, no sixth shaping, seventh hearing, tenth hand, eleventh arithmetic or eighth opening and no slate opened within reach of the basket. Dramatic purpose: the surgeon takes the body in its old order — one stiff brown-edged barley crust gone into old horn two inches from the ear with its corner a hair off the wool, the fold found where put in the empty place and still a finding, the thread frozen and unwiped, cold stopping at cheek, temple and the small bare wrist-joint as at the end of a line written out for it, the Afterdrop waiting past a warming nobody here will perform — and the infant's three wants quarrel without verdict, both true, the second louder, neither winning, the quarrel the work (T060/T086/T097). Answer 421 comes out and is filed on the sixth place; the count reaches 423 exact, six months and two hundred and forty-three days, told by nobody, and he does not stand the number up as a threshold or lay the twelve old arithmetics and the two readings gone up the road across one another, for paper is not a payer (T071/T072). Sella's whole hearth grammar holds at the morning: fire before basket, coals told the thaw and turned with a broken pot's back, intake/hold/letting-go with neither gap figured, finger along the top of the loaf shelf so the charcoal stays unread, lips on a two-gapped row, one glance at the cold clay jar with the hand half over nothing and the little-door burn closing on air, widow's mark untouched because a Ninthday morning is not an opening, twice-mended pot lifted thumb-first with the hairline showing and both proverbs to pot and fire, dressed grain turned under wool unfigured, pot rim two inches beyond the reaching hand with a half-beat and no look toward the bed, nineteen steps at the half-pace, seven walked-around places once and not twice, widest at the returning-line place, fold righted with no second fold (T058/T079/T100, T009/T013/T092, T098). Tarn keeps six where the house can check and the seventh at the lip, tells the wood *Six counted. The next I don't count* once and not twice, and lets his hand go over blade and sill and away with no breath held; Jorra parts dusty forearms from clean as clot from vessel, speaks to the wheel before any person, withholds the full note three turns ahead from any master up from High Kiln, and takes his bent finger out of the cold damper without a second holding of Ash 26; *he's not Vail* stays sealed and the promise neither given nor withdrawn (T036/T076, T035/T031/T062). Costs come as directions and go away as weather and leave no entry. Image that ends the scene: the pot rim stands two inches beyond the reaching hand with a half-beat and no look toward the bed, while the fire keeps four low pulls with the fifth unsupplied.

scenes.title: What the Twenty-ninth Left
scenes.synopsis: Second entry, no new dated heading: Ilmen 29 afternoon through the going of the light and the small hours closing the day, with answer 422 filed and the count at 423 exact, six months and two hundred and forty-three days told by nobody. Present: Corin/Dan, Sella Vail, Tarn, Jorra Vail; Garl Vail in objects. Walk-ons at the ordinary Ninthday grammar; Ilva offstage with her strip in her sleeve and her ninth hand nine, not made a reader by a reach in an empty yard. The offered figure, the asking answered with the weather, the second man's turned slate and direction, the clerk's entered figure and the fifth shaping stay found where put and are not repeated on a day that earned only its twenty-ninth; no collector comes up or down the clay road, no sixth of anything stands, and Ilmen 30 waits one morning off as a date and is not brought. Day already dated in Scene 1. Dramatic purpose: the boy takes the yard's small sounds first because they do not lie and the large ones are mostly weather — pail on the flat stone, the rope settling into its knot with the cold-stiffened rasp, a loaf pushed a finger's width along a board and stopped with nobody calling the stopping a figure — and goes once around the seven walked-around places with a look and a wide step and no number, widest at the returning-line place where a hand went in on Seed 15 and did not come back (T098, T009/T013/T092). The trough stands bare and dark with the gone pan's shallow round print on a place of its own; at the Vail corner the clean dark line keeps its finer grey called the thaw beside the called-gone ridge with a finger between, a thing left in place not a thing forgiven, and the air off the river is less cold at one edge where the low note runs nearer under the skin — found where put, called weather, not looked twice, not a sign, a fourth covering or a payment (T083/T085/T092 held). A number in a shut fist goes toward the well, looks at the light and returns into a sleeve and arrives nowhere; a woman sent to ask a pot's cost gets a note and not a price; the dressed grain lies covered and unfigured and no signature stands between figure and price (T077). The offered figure and its return stay on their own place beside Ilva's ninth hand and the fifth shaping, not offered again, not spent, not a witness (T080 held). At the going of the light Sella comes to the hearth before the basket, tells the coals it was the thaw, lifts the twice-mended pot thumb-first with the hairline showing, says *The fire doesn't know you're sorry. Feed it* once and not twice, turns the dressed grain under wool, sets the pot rim two inches beyond the reaching hand, carries him up the nineteen steps at the half-pace, sets him under the roof and never in the Debt Loft, and adds no second fold. In the small hours the towel comes out as instruments do when a case is done; six hearings stand beside and never among with the seventh empty and the Drawing's knock outside, nine record-first hands stand with no tenth, the keeping at the fold is found where put, and he does not wipe the thread or lift the crust. Image that ends the scene: the hand outside the wool comes up an inch toward the river's note, the inch not a reach, holds the interval whole on the note's own finishing, lets it go and comes straight down and lays itself flat against the fold as a man puts away a tool where the next hand will find it without looking, and there is no next hand in the room.

scenes.title: The Third Reading
scenes.synopsis: Third entry and the second dated \daymark{424}{Ilmen 30, Y.H. 814, Tenthday}: small hours opening on the hand laid down on answer 422 and the count exact at 423, first light, the carrying-down, and Ilmen 30's third and last Account-day and market, earned by its own morning. Present: Corin/Dan, Sella Vail, Tarn at the kindling, Jorra Vail at the wheel-shed edge before the carrying-down; Berr Clay comes up short off the clay road to the reading block under the moot-post; Hessa Rale takes a slate up the road toward Greybank before noon; Garl Vail in objects. Walk-ons at the two hundred, eight pigs over the wet boards, a Sill assessor writing them down, a man with a number in a shut fist sent to a slate at the watch, and the soft-cuffed clerk reported — never seen — at the out-of-line landing below the north bridge. Dramatic purpose: the surgeon takes the body in its old order and the infant's three wants quarrel without verdict (T060/T086/T097). Sella sets the basket in the moot-post's finger's width of shade where no slate lay and stands half a pace off through the reading and the bell, giving no instruction and no reason to the basket; the widow's mark stays untouched, for a market and a reading are not openings and seven openings in seven months are seven and not a rule (T058/T079). Berr wipes his thumb twice before touching nothing, holds the narrow slate unopened to his forearm, passes a finger over the figure through his sleeve, reads *One in twelve, as the notice says* twice over the basket — once for the moot and once for the households that came late — calls the levy, denies it with *your house*, never *I*, sends the number from fist to mouth to shoulder into a slate at the watch, says something low to the block about kindness being entered, and goes off up the clay road with the box locked and the third subtraction inside, believing he has done a kindness with no anger and no triumph. **Three readings of the year now stand behind one unsigned figure — three are three and not one account, the first is not made a thirteenth by the second or third, the figure read is still not the figure paid, no signature stands on the space and no doctrine comes out of three** — and neither the twelve old arithmetics nor the two earlier readings are laid across the third to make a row come out even, for paper is not a payer and the key went up in a coat pocket that never comes back down (T015/T041/T047). Hessa carries the slate edge-on and unread and is not made a reader by three figures; her eighth hand stays eighth (T080). The bell goes four, four and a gap with nobody crossing himself, the heard bell kept beside the told with both gaps in their own squares and three counts in three places staying three (T078). Answer 423 comes out on the sixth place; the count reaches 424 exact, six months and two hundred and forty-four days, told by nobody. Image that ends the scene: Berr's narrow slate goes up the clay road with its writing turned to his sleeve while the bell's fourth stroke falls into a gap nobody fills.

scenes.title: What the Thirtieth Left
scenes.synopsis: Fourth entry, no new dated heading: Ilmen 30 afternoon through the going of the light and the small hours closing the day, with answer 424 filed and the count at 424 exact, six months and two hundred and forty-four days told by nobody. Present: Corin/Dan, Sella Vail, Tarn, Jorra Vail; Garl Vail in objects. Berr gone up the clay road with the box locked; Hessa up the road unread; the soft-cuffed clerk still reported at the out-of-line landing, never a sighting, a witness or a tenth hand. The chapter's plant, years ahead and unspent: the first reaching of the adult romance at the Ilmen 30 market — a woman with clay under her nails and a pale cord-mark on the back of one hand turns a cup a quarter at a market board and sets it back where it stood, and a foundling at the edge turns his head a half-beat after a note. Two sightings on separate trays, never Fenna or Ulda in the narration, no loaf, slate, sale or word passing, no eighth of either, no name spoken over either, joined to nothing and paid by nothing; T050/T051 and T033/T034 advanced and NOT paid, the green at the pot board and the shape at the market's edge staying facts from earlier chapters and no fourth sighting made a cause. Day already dated in Scene 3. Dramatic purpose: afternoon small sounds first because they do not lie and the large ones are mostly weather; the seven walked-around places once and not twice with a look and a wide step and no number, widest at the returning-line place; the trough bare and dark with the gone pan's round print on a place of its own, not laid across the loaf's stopping or the ridge; the clean dark line and its finer grey called the thaw kept beside the called-gone grey with a finger between, and the softening at the river's skin found where put and called weather, not a sign, not a fourth covering, not made again (T098, T009/T013/T092, T083/T085/T092 held). Costs arrive as directions and go away as weather: the fist goes toward the well, looks at the light and returns into the sleeve and arrives nowhere; the woman sent for a pot's cost gets a note and not a price (T077). The three likenesses of Slate Row — the first man's face, the second man's direction and turned slate, the asking answered with the weather — go on their own trays with a finger between every pair beside the clerk's entered figure and the fifth shaping; the offered figure and its return stay where put, not made a price or a custom by a reading, and Ilva stays offstage with her ninth hand nine (T080/T090/T102 held, nothing paid). Tarn's withheld sentence is found where put and not made a habit; Jorra's promise is neither given nor withdrawn; the green and the shape stay sightings with no eighth. At the going of the light Sella keeps the whole grammar and carries him home at the half-pace, saying nothing of what was read, of the bell's gap or of the two sightings. In the small hours the towel comes out, six hearings stand with the seventh empty, nine hands with no tenth, the offered figure keeps its own place beside the ninth hand and the fifth shaping, and the hand comes down flat on the fold. Image that ends the scene: a cup stands a quarter turned on a market board and the foundling's head stops in the middle of a half-beat, both on places that do not touch, with no name and no eighth of either.

scenes.title: The First Morning of Silt
scenes.synopsis: Fifth entry and the third dated \daymark{425}{Silt 1, Y.H. 814, Firstday}: small hours opening on the hand laid down on answer 424 and the count exact at 424, six months and two hundred and forty-four days told by nobody, then first light and the morning of the first day of Silt, come on without a boundary drawn and with neither of the district's two habits of naming its months set right or left. Present: Corin/Dan, Sella Vail, Tarn at the kindling, Jorra Vail at the wheel-shed edge; Garl Vail in objects. Walk-ons at the ordinary Firstday grammar; no market, Cross, bell, Account-day, called collector or runner, and nothing from Ilmen 30's reading or its two sightings crosses under the roof as sign, lesson, mending, cause, payment or payer; Silt 10 (Day 434), the month's first reading and the year's fourth, stands nine mornings off as a date and is not brought. New day, new date, no recap. Dramatic purpose: the surgeon takes the body in its old order — crust gone into old horn two inches from the ear with its hair-lifted corner, fold found where put and still a finding, thread frozen and unwiped, cold stopping at cheek, temple and the small bare wrist-joint as at the end of a line written out for it, the Afterdrop waiting past a warming nobody here will perform — and the infant's three wants quarrel without verdict, both true, the second louder, neither winning (T060/T086/T097). Silt is taken up as though nothing had turned: fire before basket, coals told the thaw and turned with a broken pot's back, intake/hold/letting-go with neither gap figured, finger above the unread charcoal, lips on a two-gapped row, one glance at the cold clay jar with the hand half over nothing, widow's mark untouched because a new month's first tending day is not an opening and seven openings in seven months are seven and not a rule, twice-mended pot thumb-first with the hairline showing and both proverbs to pot and fire, dressed grain turned under wool unfigured, pot rim two inches beyond the reaching hand with a half-beat and no look toward the bed, nineteen steps at the half-pace, seven walked-around places once and not twice, fold righted with no second fold (T058/T079/T100, T009/T013/T092). Answer 425 comes out on the sixth place; the count reaches 425 exact, six months and two hundred and forty-five days, told by nobody, and he stands no number up as a threshold and borrows no payer from the three readings gone up the road, for paper is not a payer (T071/T072). At the yard well the softening at the river's skin is found where put and called weather, not made a fourth covering or a sign on a new month (T083/T085/T092 held). Image that ends the scene: the dressed grain lies covered under wool with no figure or handful, and the pot rim stands two inches beyond the reaching hand with the half-beat unmeasured.

scenes.title: What the First Left
scenes.synopsis: Sixth and final entry, chapter close, no new dated heading: Silt 1 afternoon through the going of the light and the small hours closing the chapter, with answer 426 filed and the count at 425 exact, six months and two hundred and forty-five days told by nobody. Present: Corin/Dan, Sella Vail; Garl Vail in objects. Offstage with keepings found where put: Tarn at kindling and flagstones with the sentence held and the loan uncalled; Jorra at the wheel-shed and cold damper with the promise neither given nor withdrawn; Ilva with her strip in her sleeve and her ninth hand nine, the offered figure and its return on their own place beside the fifth shaping; Hessa's slate unread up the road with her eighth hand eighth; Berr up the clay road with the box locked and the third subtraction inside; the soft-cuffed clerk's inward slate and entered figure reported at the out-of-line landing; the three likenesses of Slate Row and the well-asking answered with the weather on their own trays with a finger between every pair; the two market sightings of Ilmen 30 on separate trays with no eighth of either; the fifth shaping on its own tray; the softening at the river's skin kept as weather; the green at the pot board and the shape at the market's edge as sightings with no eighth. Walk-ons only at the yard grammar. No second well-telling, no repetition of the offered figure, no market, no present-tense break and no \memory{} tag; no sixth hearing, tenth hand, tenth stopping, eighth opening, sixth shaping, eleventh arithmetic, signature, payer, witness or reader. Day already dated in Scene 5. Dramatic purpose: afternoon small sounds first because they do not lie and the large ones are mostly weather; the seven walked-around places once and not twice with a look and a wide step and no number, widest at the returning-line place; the trough bare and dark with the gone pan's round print on a place of its own; costs arrive as directions and go away as weather and leave no entry (T077, T098, T009/T013/T092 held). The surgeon's exactness and the infant's want stand side by side and neither buys the other; under them, louder, the wanting goes on — the crust lifted, the thread wiped, a hand on the pot handle — and gets none of the three. Both are true, the second is louder, neither wins, no verdict is looked for and the quarrel is the work (T060/T086/T097). In the small hours the towel comes out at the head of the bed as instruments do when a case is done; six hearings of the full note stand beside and never among with the seventh place empty and the Drawing's flat knock outside on its own ground, the heard bell keeps its square beside the told with both gaps in their own squares, three counts in three places stay three, nine record-first hands stand with no tenth and nine stoppings with no tenth, and three readings stand behind one unsigned figure with three being three and not one account and no signature on the space. Answer 426 comes out exact, complete, worth nothing at two inches of air, a restraint and not a payment borrowing no house count and supplying no payer. Four hundred and twenty-five exact, six months and two hundred and forty-five days, told by nobody who would have known what a number counted; he does not stand it up as a threshold or figure and borrows no payer from the arithmetics gone up the road. No eighth opening, seventh hearing, sixth shaping, tenth hand, tenth stopping, eleventh arithmetic, signature, payer, witness or reader stands on any of the three days, and the unsent call to Nina is not paid again (T020 held). Image that ends the scene and pulls forward: the hand outside the wool comes up an inch toward the river's note under the finger's-width door, the inch not a reach, takes a small intake from the room whose floor does not touch his, holds the interval whole on the note's own finishing, lets it go as the note ends and comes straight down and lays itself flat against the fold as a man puts away a tool where the next hand will find it without looking, and he does not wipe the thread and does not lift the crust; the well gives back the weather, the house goes on, and Silt 2 (Day 426) waits in a morning not yet lived and not brought into a day that has earned only its first.
